title: BaseLocalizationDLinearGlue
statement: Let E, F and D be commutative rings, phi : E isomorphic to F a ring isomorphism, p : E to D and q : F to D ring homomorphisms such that q composed with phi is p. Let M be an E-module and N an F-module, and let g be an invertible E-linear map from M to N restricted along phi. There is a D-linear isomorphism from D tensor_E M to D tensor_F N sending 1 tensor x to 1 tensor g(x) for every x in M.

proof.text:
the ring isomorphism makes restriction of scalars an equivalence, so
its scalar-extension counit is invertible. Extend g and compose with that
counit to obtain an F-linear isomorphism from F tensor_E M to N. Extend this
isomorphism along q to D. Tensor associativity identifies its source with
D tensor_E M, since q composed with phi equals p. On 1 tensor x, the
associator gives 1 tensor (1 tensor x), the extension of g gives
1 tensor (1 tensor g(x)), and the counit gives 1 tensor g(x).
This uses no flatness of D and applies to zero rings and zero modules.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0DJ8 affine localization identity; Tag 06Y6 universal counit and localization tensor identity

mathlib_searches.query: Derived tensor with an algebra over a localization agrees with derived tensor over the localized base
Derived tensor product commutes with localization of the base ring

lean.statement: theorem exists_extendScalars_iso_of_ringEquiv {E F D : Type u} [CommRing E] [CommRing F] [CommRing D] (φ : E ≃+* F) (p : E →+* D) (q : F →+* D) (h : q.comp φ.toRingHom = p) (M : ModuleCat.{u} E) (N : ModuleCat.{u} F) (g : M ⟶ (restrictScalars φ.toRingHom).obj N) (hg : IsIso g) : ∃ e : (extendScalars p).obj M ≅ (extendScalars q).obj N, ∀ x : M, e.hom ((1 : D) ⊗ₜ[E,p] x) = (1 : D) ⊗ₜ[F,q] g x
